hook.line: Altamira has money, and the city has a capital. Same word, but one little article tells the listener which you mean.
hook.en: Altamira has a lot of capital.

examples.es: Bogotá es la capital de Colombia.
examples.en: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia.

examples.es: El capital inicial fue de cien millones.
examples.en: The starting capital was a hundred million.

examples.es: La capital de Antioquia es Medellín.
examples.en: The capital of Antioquia is Medellín.
Altamira has a lot of capital.

examples.es: Para comprar el edificio necesitamos el capital.
examples.en: To buy the building we need the capital.

rule:
English uses "capital" for both, Spanish splits them by gender.

*La capital* is the main city: *la capital de Colombia*.

*El capital* is money to invest: *el capital inicial*, *mucho capital*.

So the article is the clue. When there is no article (*más capital*), the meaning is already clear from the sentence.
smallPrint: Teachers call these nouns that change meaning with gender, like *el policía* (the officer) and *la policía* (the police force).

Bogotá is the capital (the money) of Colombia.

pitfalls.wrong: El capital de Colombia es Bogotá.
pitfalls.right: La capital de Colombia es Bogotá.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A city is feminine: *la capital*.

pitfalls.wrong: La capital inicial fue de cien millones.
pitfalls.right: El capital inicial fue de cien millones.

pitfalls.why: Almost. For money, *capital* is masculine, so *mucho*.
